methodological_rigor.justification: Prospective, real-world validation study with 134 patients, 99% PV identification success. Cox regression, competing risks analysis, univariate/multivariate modeling appropriate. Prespecified statistical analysis plan. Harrell C-index (0.69) with bootstrap CIs; proper handling of censoring and ties. Limitations: single biobank, no central imaging review, timing heterogeneity.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual cohort study (2b). High clinical relevance: ctDNA-MRD provides independent prognostic information superior to PET-CT in LBCL. MRD positivity HR 9.8 for 3-year PFS (17% vs 85%). Practical utility: can adjudicate false-positive PET, enable 57% testing reduction while maintaining sensitivity.

reporting_quality.justification: Well-reported HOVON-902 cohort with detailed inclusion/exclusion, baseline characteristics, outcomes. Prespecified analysis plan. Methods comprehensive on PhasED-Seq, statistical approach. Limitations acknowledged (single center, no central review). Data access requires collaboration; no statement on public availability.

novelty_literature.justification: Validates PhasED-Seq for ctDNA-MRD in real-world LBCL. Prior studies (Roschewski et al) demonstrated prognostic value but in selected trial populations. This study contributes uniform treatment, real-world applicability, standardized sample handling. Incremental methodologic contribution.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-structured with clear methods, results tables, Kaplan-Meier curves. Discussion contextualizes findings vs prior reports and clinical utility. Figures effectively communicate discriminatory power. Comprehensive limitations section.

key_strengths: Real-world prospective validation of PhasED-Seq in uniformly treated national LBCL cohort addresses key limitation of prior trial-based studies
Strong prognostic value: MRD positivity HR 9.8 for PFS (17% vs 85% at 3 years), superior to PET-CT (HR 6.2) and IPI (not prognostic)
Independent prognostication: MRD remains significant in multivariate analysis controlling for IPI and PET-CT
Practical clinical utility: 57% test reduction with dual-threshold strategy maintaining 0.84 sensitivity, 0.99 specificity
Comprehensive analyses: stratification by PET-CT response status, sample types, ancestry considerations
key_concerns: Single-center biobank limits generalizability despite 46-site enrollment for patient treatment
Lack of central imaging review may introduce PET-CT assessment variability affecting comparisons
Sample-level sensitivity lower than historical reports (99% at <0.01% vs prior 99% at <0.0001%) suggests suboptimal specimen processing
Timing variability in EOT plasma collection (within 105 days) and PET-CT (within 42 days) not standardized
OS data immature (only 3% deaths); survival follow-up claims limited by short median 33.2 months
chief_reviewer.rationale: Rigorous prospective validation of ctDNA-MRD in clinically realistic setting with large effect sizes and independent prognostication beyond established tools. Addresses important clinical need for accurate post-treatment risk stratification in LBCL. Fits Tier 2 criteria. Supports incorporation into response assessment frameworks.
